findings.title: Deleted-project notes can remain eligible for retrieval through an orphaned bot project identity
findings.expected: Missing projects and archived/temporary conversations must not be eligible for fleet context.
findings.changed: Worker pauses orphan project runs before reading context; local scope independently excludes archived and temporary chats and archived notes.

findings.title: Browser scheduling is not equivalent to persistent automation
findings.expected: Distinguish an open-browser worker, runnable local worker scripts, and verified hosted automation.
findings.changed: Recovered correction confirms schedule:tick/schedule:worker already exist. UI now describes browser or running local worker; hosted deployment remains external-required.
remaining: No hosted worker was installed, deployed, or proven continuously running.

findings.title: Missed scheduled occurrences are collapsed without an explicit recovery policy
findings.expected: Missed occurrences and overlaps need explicit policy, anchored cadence and individual outcomes.
findings.changed: Added once/skip/review recovery, one-time authorized catch-up, wait/skip/bounded-parallel overlap, latest 100 occurrence records with independent run outcomes and UI.
remaining: Automatic replay of every missed occurrence is intentionally not implemented. Latest 100 occurrence records are retained.

findings.title: Overlapping scheduled runs can lose their individual schedule-level outcome tracking

remaining: Automatic replay of every missed occurrence is intentionally not implemented. Latest 100 occurrence records are retained.

findings.title: Scheduled conversation execution does not inherently continue the conversation
findings.expected: Separate bot workflows and autonomous conversation continuation; explicitly select result destination.
findings.changed: Implemented honest bot-task semantics and optional idempotent completed-result delivery to the original saved conversation; default remains Runs. Missing/archived destination records a delivery error and never substitutes or resurrects a chat. Archive restore/import resets delivery to Runs; merging preserves the local explicitly selected conversation and cannot redirect it from archive data.
remaining: Autonomous model-driven conversation continuation, monitoring, and reminders remain separate modes requiring provider/cost/worker and delivery contracts. No hidden model call was added.

findings.title: Saved execution plans are not authoritative during fleet execution
findings.expected: Execute the saved allowed plan, enforce dependencies and transfer declared typed results; unfinished work cannot be completed merely by exhausting a budget.
findings.changed: Worker executes saved steps, rechecks current capability/project, validates prior receipts and inputFrom output/recordIds, captures typed result IDs, and marks exhausted partial plans failed.

findings.title: Fleet planning is a tool-list expansion rather than objective-driven intelligence
findings.expected: An explicit supported objective should choose relevant allowed tools and unknown/ambiguous goals should remain truthfully labeled.
findings.changed: Local deterministic intent selection narrows saved tool plans; unavailable explicit requested capabilities refuse instead of substituting an unrelated workflow; ambiguous goals preserve labeled template sequence.
remaining: This is a bounded deterministic planner, not general model-generated planning or autonomous reasoning.

findings.title: Search scans workspace content synchronously whenever its dependencies change
findings.expected: Repeated queries must reuse normalized workspace text and project/context metadata, rebuilding only affected immutable collections while preserving complete message matches and ranking.
findings.changed: Added a component-scoped reusable palette index builder with one latest snapshot per collection, weak message-object normalization cache, incremental collection/context rebuilds and no persistent per-query cache. CommandApp memoizes transformed chat metadata and the search index separately from query/keyboard state. Querying retains independent-term and exact-phrase matching, every matching message ID, exact-title priority and first matching excerpt, without a redundant title-only result.
remaining: Queries still synchronously scan already-normalized index records; no worker-thread latency or live-device performance guarantee is claimed. Cache size follows the current workspace snapshot; prior snapshots/query results are not retained. Immutable collection/record updates are required and match current workspace state handling.

findings.title: Persistence readiness does not establish verified backup availability
findings.expected: Storage configuration, backup existence and proven restoration are separate claims.
findings.changed: Storage identity and archive coverage manifest are explicit. Runtime cloudBackup/restartChecked remain false. Synthetic archive restore coverage exercises declared workspace data categories.
remaining: Production backup schedule, protected backup destination, RPO/RTO and durable verification record require an infrastructure policy and later authorized live run.

findings.title: Browser and server synchronization uses a binary content-presence decision
findings.expected: Bootstrap must preserve both nonempty copies; subsequent saves require revision-aware compare-and-swap.
findings.changed: Existing chooseServerSync is conservative bootstrap. Full use-mind-workspace caller already reads serverRevision and sends expectedRevision. Source trace and bootstrap regressions confirm this; new disk/CAS fixture remains separately tracked.
remaining: The AA134 isolated disk fixture now proves stale compare-and-swap refusal after database reopen. No live server/account synchronization was tested.

findings.title: A configured remote database does not establish restart recovery
findings.expected: Persist a synthetic full workspace/control state, close the database, reopen it, and prove isolation and stale-write rejection.
findings.changed: Added and passed the normal-runner file-persist regression: isolated disk-backed PGlite closes and reopens; occurrence/run plan, deletion tombstones, control state, owner isolation and stale compare-and-swap rejection survive. Existing conversation reopen regression also passes.
remaining: This is synthetic local disk/PGlite recovery, not a live hosted PostgreSQL restart, production backup or physical-device proof. The constrained implementation environment needed workspace TMPDIR and Node --max-old-space-size=256; earlier unbounded attempts were SIGKILLed at about 1,059 MB RSS.

findings.title: Local persistence terminology is internally inconsistent
findings.expected: Storage labels distinguish disk file from process memory without breaking old wire clients.
findings.changed: Added storageKind local-file/remote-postgres/refused; retained legacy backend alias for compatibility and kept independent unverified durability flags.

findings.title: Backup completeness remains unverified across Adrian's major data categories
findings.expected: The workspace export declares portable categories and omissions, and recovery preserves execution safety.
findings.changed: Archive manifest inventories content, versions/tombstones, agent/run/schedule records, labels, recovery records, usage and media portability. Synthetic pack/unpack/restore fixture verifies major categories and disabled/paused execution restore behavior.
remaining: Whole-account backup excludes API/OAuth secrets, server-only receipts, out-of-workspace browser preferences, unavailable blob bytes and external video content. This is not verified cloud backup.
